title: Bittensor Daily News: November 21, 2026

updates.headline: SN3 Teutonic announces a 5% Gamma allocation to SN51 Lium
updates.summary:
SN3 Teutonic’s team announced on November 20 that it is directing 5% of emissions through Gamma to SN51 Lium for research and experimental compute. The stated distribution is 18% to the owner, 41% to validators, 36% to miners and 5% to SN51 Lium.

The team says the compute will support experiments in training, evaluation and model improvement. For readers following Gamma, the practical distinction is an allocation intended to fund another subnet’s service, rather than a general token-market purchase announced without a service purpose.

This report verifies the original team announcement. The complete finalized allocation event, amounts converted and subsequent GPU-credit consumption have not been independently reconciled, so the announced percentages should not be read as proof of delivered compute or measured revenue.
updates.ratingReason: Four stars: a concrete announced cross-subnet compute-funding allocation changes the use of emissions, exceeding routine three-star competition changes. Five is not established by this bounded allocation.

updates.headline: SN24 ms.computer plans a website competition with 2,424 alpha in prizes
updates.summary:
SN24 ms.computer’s team said on November 20 that it was aiming to open a website-building competition on November 21, with three winners sharing 2,424 SN24 alpha. The challenge is to build a site, host it on ms.computer and show the result.

The team clarified that participation is open to everyone, including miners, and requires no miner-software update. Entry details were still to be announced in the messages reviewed. Its public getting-started page describes a command-line build-and-deploy workflow and access to a free token.

The news is the planned competition and participation terms. Free hosting was already covered in the November 16 edition; this is not presented as a new first launch, and the prize announcement is not an emission-split change.
updates.ratingReason: Three stars under the competition cap: a concrete prize pool and entry scope are useful participation news. Two would understate the announced event; four would overstate it.

updates.headline: SN55 NIOME warns users about malicious emails using its name
updates.summary:
SN55 NIOME issued an urgent warning on November 21 at 7:51 AM Eastern, saying it had reason to believe people were receiving malicious emails appearing to come from contact@genomes.io. The team asked recipients not to click messages from that address and directed questions to its official X account and Telegram group.

The verified fact is the team’s warning. Its post does not establish how the emails were sent, whether the mailbox itself was compromised, or whether any recipient lost funds. Those questions should not be answered by inference from the sender name.
updates.ratingReason: Three stars: an actionable team warning affects users, beyond minor housekeeping. Four is not established without a verified broader incident or consequence.

updates.headline: SN66 Conjectures publishes a degree-four minimal-graph proof
updates.summary:
SN66 Conjectures announced on November 20 that a miner submission rules out non-affine polynomial minimal graphs of degree at most four in every dimension. In plain terms, within that polynomial degree limit, a graph satisfying the minimal-surface equation must be flat. The project credits the solver JenW1N and publishes a Lean proof alongside an explanatory paper dated November 16. This is a dated catch-up to yesterday’s missed announcement.

The paper identifies the remaining mathematical contribution as excluding degree-four solutions in dimensions eight and above. It explicitly makes no priority claim after a bounded literature review. The result does not by itself resolve the unrestricted question for every polynomial degree, and non-polynomial minimal graphs are outside its scope.

Conjectures describes the submission as formally verified. This review inspected the announcement and explanatory paper but did not independently rerun the Lean checker. The paper also distinguishes its AI-assisted prose exposition from the formal source that establishes the checked theorem.
updates.ratingReason: Four stars: a specific formal result with a public proof artifact exceeds routine research commentary. Five is not established without wider independently assessed significance; this is not the unrestricted problem.

ratingAssessment.consequence: Four stars: a specific formal result with a public proof artifact exceeds routine research commentary. Five is not established without wider independently assessed significance; this is not the unrestricted problem.
ratingAssessment.evidence: Official November 20 result announcement; Explanatory paper dated November 16; Published formal solution
ratingAssessment.scope: Degree-at-most-four polynomial minimal graphs in all dimensions.
ratingAssessment.uncertainty: Lean verification attributed to the project; not independently rerun.
ratingAssessment.adjacentRatingReason: Four stars: a specific formal result with a public proof artifact exceeds routine research commentary. Five is not established without wider independently assessed significance; this is not the unrestricted problem.

updates.headline: SN75 Hippius case study details SN91 Cascade infrastructure migration
updates.summary:
A November 20 case study from SN75 Hippius says SN91 Cascade now uses its object storage, model registry and managed PostgreSQL database. The article quotes Cascade founder Chris Hames describing the migration and the three services in use. This is a dated catch-up to a development missing from yesterday’s edition.

The reported stack has specific jobs: S3-compatible storage holds training records and a public audit log; Hippius Hub distributes models and generator containers; and the managed database supports Cascade’s Ephemeris forecasting API. The database previously ran on Supabase.

The case study reports roughly 66% lower storage costs and 33% lower database costs for this migration. Those are supplier-published, customer-attributed figures, not independently audited invoices or savings every customer can assume. GitHub Actions runners and Confidential VMs are described as planned additions, not services already in this deployment.
updates.ratingReason: Four stars: a named customer describes concrete use of three infrastructure services, beyond a routine product update. Five is not supported by this bounded case study.

updates.headline: SN94 Cathedral expands Escape rooms and clarifies compute intake
updates.summary:
In a November 20 follow-up to its previously covered validator update, SN94 Cathedral’s team described five simultaneous Escape rooms, limited to one per player, and said the payout mechanism was enabled. That is an operating update from the team, not independent confirmation that a participant has received a payout.

For the separate compute intake, the team said applicants would be reviewed over the weekend and whitelisted based on suitability. It had not specified a deposit requirement, a final initial-miner count or customer-utilization figures in the exchange reviewed. Pricing offers would follow application review.

The additional room capacity and intake clarification are the new details. The stable12 release and initial call for compute applications were covered yesterday.

updates.headline: SN105 Beam adds one-click Studio deployment on Azure
updates.summary:
SN105 Beam announced on November 20 that customers can deploy Beam Studio into their own Microsoft Azure subscription through a prepared deployment template. Its documentation describes a dedicated virtual machine, data disk and network, with Studio installed automatically. This follows the previously covered AWS option.

The customer owns and pays for the Azure resources. The guide estimates about $81 a month for its default East US configuration, including disks and a public IP; that is a documented estimate, not a universal quote. Transfers continue to use the Beam network. The guide offers HTTPS access or a private SSH-tunnel mode, with different feature limits.

This is a documented deployment route, not evidence of a Microsoft partnership or paid customer adoption. The template and instructions were inspected without creating cloud resources or running a transfer.
updates.ratingReason: Four stars: a substantive deployment path makes the product available in another major cloud environment, beyond minor maintenance. Five is not supported by the limited launch scope; Azure availability is not a strategic partnership.

updates.headline: SN111 Claims revises its extraction competition and delays testnet opening
updates.summary:
SN111 Claims is replacing its current mainnet extraction round with a new v1.1 schema. The team’s November 20 schedule set mainnet submissions for November 22 at 18:00 UTC and evaluation for November 23 at 12:00 UTC. On November 21 at 9:16 AM Eastern, it said the testnet was not ready and was targeting an opening at 18:00 UTC that day, superseding the earlier noon-UTC submission target.

The revised extraction format combines a JSON result with separate CSV numerical tables. Scoring is intended to measure whether findings faithfully represent the source paper, including values, relationships and context. The team said the scorer was implemented on November 21; unresolved validator judgments can put a paper on hold rather than automatically scoring it zero.

The miner inference cap remains $0.10 per paper. Initial rounds use the main paper without supplementary material and start from the reference miner rather than the old incumbent. Execution limits and the actual testnet opening still required confirmation at this review.
updates.ratingReason: Three stars under the competition cap: schema, scoring and timing materially affect participants. Two would understate that change; four would overrate a routine competition revision.

updates.headline: SN120 Affine plans stricter batch checks and deduplication
updates.summary:
Const said in SN120 Affine’s official channel on November 21 that stricter batch checks and deduplication were being added, responding to a participant request. This is a planned processing improvement, not confirmation that reported queue problems have been resolved.

Separately, Const described SN120 Affine on X that morning as open recursive self-improvement. That is his characterization of the approach, not a new benchmark result or independently measured capability.

ecosystem.headline: Runtime 493 puts Gamma spending under the customer hotkey
ecosystem.summary:
The Subtensor repository released runtime 493 on November 20 with a new way to spend Gamma service credits. Under the released design, the deposit’s own hotkey signs a fee-free spend directed to a listed service. The service reads the accumulated spending record and credits the customer, instead of holding separate authority to spend the customer’s deposit. The coldkey retains control over the balance, daily spending limit and closure.

For developers, this is a breaking interface change. The separate spender field and its setter are removed, several call arguments and indices change, and the Gamma runtime API moves to version 2. A zero daily cap pauses spending; otherwise the minimum cap is 0.1 Gamma. New deposits created through Gamma emissions start paused until the owner sets a cap.

The published release and merged implementation are verified. This edition has not independently verified its Finney activation block. Burning Gamma credits when they are spent is not a claim that an additional alpha-token burn occurs at that step, and the release itself does not establish customer adoption.
ecosystem.ratingReason: Four stars: a network-wide change to payment authority and integration interfaces exceeds routine three-star maintenance. Five is not established by this bounded protocol release.

ratingAssessment.consequence: Four stars: a network-wide change to payment authority and integration interfaces exceeds routine three-star maintenance. Five is not established by this bounded protocol release.

ratingAssessment.scope: Released Gamma spending design and migration requirements.
